label: UniFi G2 Starter Kit
description: UniFi G2 Starter Kit (UA-G2-SK) - 5x 1G RJ45 (1 PoE++ input, 4 PoE+ outputs at 30 W/port, 45 W aggregate). 30 W max without PoE output, 50 W with.

poe.note: Ubiquiti prints one row for the whole PoE side on https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/door-access/ua-g2-sk: **(1) PoE++ input, 50V DC, 1A; (4) PoE outputs, 50V DC, 30W per port (Max 45W aggregated)**, with **Max. Power Consumption 30W (Without PoE output) / 50W (With PoE output)** and **Power Method PoE++**. 45 W is the PSE allocation - the total across the 4 outputs, not a per-port figure - so 4 x 30 W of cameras (120 W) exceed what this hub can supply, and the engine must refuse the last watt rather than promise 30 W a port. Same shape as `devices/ubiquiti/ua-hub.json`, which was already modelled this way.

notes: Ubiquiti tech specs `https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/door-access/ua-g2-sk` (HTTP 200, read 2026-11-20): **Networking Interface (5) 10/100/1000 Base-T**, **PoE Interface (1) PoE++ input, 50V DC, 1A; (4) PoE outputs, 50V DC, 30W per port (Max 45W aggregated)**, **Max. Power Consumption 30W (Without PoE output) / 50W (With PoE output)**, **Power Method PoE++**. **This entry used to model the uplink as the PoE port**: eth0 declared `poeOut` class PoE++ and the 4 output jacks declared nothing, so the spec advertised a 60 W source on the port that is fed *by* the switch, while the jacks a camera is actually cabled to could source nothing - and with no `poe.budgetW` the loader fell through to the model name, found no wattage and served 0 W (`node scripts/audit-poe-budget.js` listed this file under "Silent (PoE out, no budget)"). Direction now follows the vendor row: eth0 is the PoE++ PD input (50V x 1A = 50 W), eth1-eth4 are 30 W PSE outputs behind a 45 W aggregate budget. The page calls them "PoE outputs"; they are modelled `PoE+` because the same row gives 30 W per port, which is 802.3at Type 2 whatever the label. The vendor prints 10/100/1000 Base-T, so both banks gained the 10M rung.
